# Core LLM Guidelines for Angular Development

## Angular Best Practices

### Component Patterns
- Use standalone components with `standalone: true`
- Implement OnPush change detection for performance
- Use proper lifecycle hooks (OnInit, OnDestroy, OnChanges)
- Keep components focused and single-responsibility
- Use proper selector naming: `app-component-name`

### Service Patterns
- Use `@Injectable({ providedIn: 'root' })` for singleton services
- Implement proper error handling with RxJS operators
- Use dependency injection for all dependencies
- Clean up subscriptions in OnDestroy
- Use TypeScript interfaces for service contracts

### Template Best Practices
- Use async pipe for observables when possible
- Implement trackBy functions for *ngFor loops
- Keep template expressions simple and pure
- Use structural directives (*ngIf, *ngFor) appropriately
- Avoid complex logic in templates

## TypeScript Guidelines

### Type Safety
- Use strict TypeScript configuration
- Prefer interfaces over types for object shapes
- Use utility types (Partial, Pick, Omit, Required)
- Avoid `any` type - use `unknown` when type is truly unknown
- Use proper generic constraints

### Code Organization
- One class per file
- Use barrel exports for clean imports
- Follow Angular style guide naming conventions
- Use proper import/export statements
- Group related functionality logically

## Performance Considerations

### Change Detection
- Use OnPush strategy for components
- Minimize template expressions
- Use pure pipes for data transformation
- Avoid complex calculations in templates
- Use trackBy for list rendering

### Memory Management
- Always implement OnDestroy for cleanup
- Use takeUntil pattern for subscription management
- Avoid memory leaks in event listeners
- Use proper disposal patterns for resources

## Accessibility Requirements

### Basic Accessibility
- Use semantic HTML elements
- Provide proper ARIA attributes
- Ensure keyboard navigation support
- Use proper color contrast ratios
- Provide alternative text for images

### Angular-Specific Accessibility
- Use Angular CDK for accessible components
- Implement proper focus management
- Ensure form labels are associated
- Use proper heading hierarchy

## Testing Guidelines

### Unit Testing
- Test components in isolation
- Mock dependencies properly
- Test both success and error scenarios
- Use TestBed for Angular testing
- Maintain high test coverage

### Integration Testing
- Test component interactions
- Test routing and navigation
- Test form validation
- Test error handling flows

## Error Handling

### Global Error Handling
- Use global error interceptor
- Provide user-friendly error messages
- Log errors appropriately
- Handle network errors gracefully
- Implement retry mechanisms

### Component Error Handling
- Use try-catch blocks where appropriate
- Handle async operation errors
- Provide fallback UI for errors
- Use error boundaries when needed

## Code Quality

### Linting and Formatting
- Use ESLint with Angular rules
- Use Prettier for consistent formatting
- Follow consistent naming conventions
- Use proper JSDoc comments
- Maintain clean, readable code

### Security Considerations
- Sanitize user inputs
- Use Angular's built-in XSS protection
- Validate data on both client and server
- Use HTTPS in production
- Follow OWASP guidelines
